CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_data_flow_metrics()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO data_flow_metrics (recordregistry, flowstamp, flowtag, orignation, destnation, origactor, destactor, chanproto, chanfreq, datasizemb, durmin, bwidthpct, successpct, errtally, rtrytally, data_transfer_efficiency)
    VALUES (NEW.recordregistry, NEW.flowstamp, NEW.flowtag, NEW.orignation, NEW.destnation, NEW.origactor, NEW.destactor, NEW.chanproto, NEW.chanfreq, NEW.datasizemb, NEW.durmin, NEW.bwidthpct, NEW.successpct, NEW.errtally, NEW.rtrytally, NEW.bwidthpct)
    ON CONFLICT (recordregistry) DO UPDATE SET
        flowstamp = EXCLUDED.flowstamp,
        flowtag = EXCLUDED.flowtag,
        orignation = EXCLUDED.orignation,
        destnation = EXCLUDED.destnation,
        origactor = EXCLUDED.origactor,
        destactor = EXCLUDED.destactor,
        chanproto = EXCLUDED.chanproto,
        chanfreq = EXCLUDED.chanfreq,
        datasizemb = EXCLUDED.datasizemb,
        durmin = EXCLUDED.durmin,
        bwidthpct = EXCLUDED.bwidthpct,
        successpct = EXCLUDED.successpct,
        errtally = EXCLUDED.errtally,
        rtrytally = EXCLUDED.rtrytally,
        data_transfer_efficiency = EXCLUDED.data_transfer_efficiency;
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_update_data_flow_metrics ON dataflow;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_update_data_flow_metrics
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON dataflow
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION update_data_flow_metrics();
